From 8f15b5071b4548b0aafc03b366eb45c9c6566704 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: David Carlier <devnexen@gmail.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 14:11:08 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] netfilter: ctnetlink: use netlink policy range checks

Replace manual range and mask validations with netlink policy
annotations in ctnetlink code paths, so that the netlink core rejects
invalid values early and can generate extack errors.

- CTA_PROTOINFO_TCP_STATE: reject values > TCP_CONNTRACK_SYN_SENT2 at
  policy level, removing the manual >= TCP_CONNTRACK_MAX check.
- CTA_PROTOINFO_TCP_WSCALE_ORIGINAL/REPLY: reject values > TCP_MAX_WSCALE
  (14). The normal TCP option parsing path already clamps to this value,
  but the ctnetlink path accepted 0-255, causing undefined behavior when
  used as a u32 shift count.
- CTA_FILTER_ORIG_FLAGS/REPLY_FLAGS: use NLA_POLICY_MASK with
  CTA_FILTER_F_ALL, removing the manual mask checks.
- CTA_EXPECT_FLAGS: use NLA_POLICY_MASK with NF_CT_EXPECT_MASK, adding
  a new mask define grouping all valid expect flags.

Extracted from a broader nf-next patch by Florian Westphal, scoped to
ctnetlink for the fixes tree.

Fixes: c8e2078cfe41 ("[NETFILTER]: ctnetlink: add support for internal tcp connection tracking flags handling")
Signed-off-by: David Carlier <devnexen@gmail.com>
Co-developed-by: Florian Westphal <fw@strlen.de>
Signed-off-by: Pablo Neira Ayuso <pablo@netfilter.org>

diff --git a/include/uapi/linux/netfilter/nf_conntrack_common.h b/include/uapi/linux/netfilter/nf_conntrack_common.h
index 26071021e986..56b6b60a814f 100644
--- a/include/uapi/linux/netfilter/nf_conntrack_common.h
+++ b/include/uapi/linux/netfilter/nf_conntrack_common.h
@@ -159,5 +159,9 @@ enum ip_conntrack_expect_events {
 #define NF_CT_EXPECT_INACTIVE		0x2
 #define NF_CT_EXPECT_USERSPACE		0x4
 
+#ifdef __KERNEL__
+#define NF_CT_EXPECT_MASK	(NF_CT_EXPECT_PERMANENT | NF_CT_EXPECT_INACTIVE | \
+				 NF_CT_EXPECT_USERSPACE)
+#endif
 
 #endif /* _UAPI_NF_CONNTRACK_COMMON_H */

diff --git a/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_proto_tcp.c b/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_proto_tcp.c
index 0c1d086e96cb..b67426c2189b 100644
--- a/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_proto_tcp.c
+++ b/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_proto_tcp.c
@@ -1385,9 +1385,9 @@ static int tcp_to_nlattr(struct sk_buff *skb, struct nlattr *nla,
 }
 
 static const struct nla_policy tcp_nla_policy[CTA_PROTOINFO_TCP_MAX+1] = {
-	[CTA_PROTOINFO_TCP_STATE]	    = { .type = NLA_U8 },
-	[CTA_PROTOINFO_TCP_WSCALE_ORIGINAL] = { .type = NLA_U8 },
-	[CTA_PROTOINFO_TCP_WSCALE_REPLY]    = { .type = NLA_U8 },
+	[CTA_PROTOINFO_TCP_STATE]	    = NLA_POLICY_MAX(NLA_U8, TCP_CONNTRACK_SYN_SENT2),
+	[CTA_PROTOINFO_TCP_WSCALE_ORIGINAL] = NLA_POLICY_MAX(NLA_U8, TCP_MAX_WSCALE),
+	[CTA_PROTOINFO_TCP_WSCALE_REPLY]    = NLA_POLICY_MAX(NLA_U8, TCP_MAX_WSCALE),
 	[CTA_PROTOINFO_TCP_FLAGS_ORIGINAL]  = { .len = sizeof(struct nf_ct_tcp_flags) },
 	[CTA_PROTOINFO_TCP_FLAGS_REPLY]	    = { .len = sizeof(struct nf_ct_tcp_flags) },
 };
@@ -1414,10 +1414,6 @@ static int nlattr_to_tcp(struct nlattr *cda[], struct nf_conn *ct)
 	if (err < 0)
 		return err;
 
-	if (tb[CTA_PROTOINFO_TCP_STATE] &&
-	    nla_get_u8(tb[CTA_PROTOINFO_TCP_STATE]) >= TCP_CONNTRACK_MAX)
-		return -EINVAL;
-
 	spin_lock_bh(&ct->lock);
 	if (tb[CTA_PROTOINFO_TCP_STATE])
 		ct->proto.tcp.state = nla_get_u8(tb[CTA_PROTOINFO_TCP_STATE]);
-- 
2.34.1



diff --git a/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_netlink.c b/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_netlink.c
index 6e6aeb0ab0a1..3f408f3713bb 100644
--- a/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_netlink.c
+++ b/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_netlink.c
@@ -910,8 +910,8 @@ struct ctnetlink_filter {
 };
 
 static const struct nla_policy cta_filter_nla_policy[CTA_FILTER_MAX + 1] = {
-	[CTA_FILTER_ORIG_FLAGS]		= { .type = NLA_U32 },
-	[CTA_FILTER_REPLY_FLAGS]	= { .type = NLA_U32 },
+	[CTA_FILTER_ORIG_FLAGS]		= NLA_POLICY_MASK(NLA_U32, CTA_FILTER_F_ALL),
+	[CTA_FILTER_REPLY_FLAGS]	= NLA_POLICY_MASK(NLA_U32, CTA_FILTER_F_ALL),
 };
 
 static int ctnetlink_parse_filter(const struct nlattr *attr,
@@ -925,17 +925,11 @@ static int ctnetlink_parse_filter(const struct nlattr *attr,
 	if (ret)
 		return ret;
 
-	if (tb[CTA_FILTER_ORIG_FLAGS]) {
+	if (tb[CTA_FILTER_ORIG_FLAGS])
 		filter->orig_flags = nla_get_u32(tb[CTA_FILTER_ORIG_FLAGS]);
-		if (filter->orig_flags & ~CTA_FILTER_F_ALL)
-			return -EOPNOTSUPP;
-	}
 
-	if (tb[CTA_FILTER_REPLY_FLAGS]) {
+	if (tb[CTA_FILTER_REPLY_FLAGS])
 		filter->reply_flags = nla_get_u32(tb[CTA_FILTER_REPLY_FLAGS]);
-		if (filter->reply_flags & ~CTA_FILTER_F_ALL)
-			return -EOPNOTSUPP;
-	}
 
 	return 0;
 }
@@ -2634,7 +2628,7 @@ static const struct nla_policy exp_nla_policy[CTA_EXPECT_MAX+1] = {
 	[CTA_EXPECT_HELP_NAME]	= { .type = NLA_NUL_STRING,
 				    .len = NF_CT_HELPER_NAME_LEN - 1 },
 	[CTA_EXPECT_ZONE]	= { .type = NLA_U16 },
-	[CTA_EXPECT_FLAGS]	= { .type = NLA_U32 },
+	[CTA_EXPECT_FLAGS]	= NLA_POLICY_MASK(NLA_BE32, NF_CT_EXPECT_MASK),
 	[CTA_EXPECT_CLASS]	= { .type = NLA_U32 },
 	[CTA_EXPECT_NAT]	= { .type = NLA_NESTED },
 	[CTA_EXPECT_FN]		= { .type = NLA_NUL_STRING },

The patch replaces manual range and mask validations in ctnetlink with netlink policy annotations, moving error handling into the netlink core for earlier rejection and better error reporting.

### Modifications per file:

- **include/uapi/linux/netfilter/nf_conntrack_common.h**:  
  Adds a new macro `NF_CT_EXPECT_MASK` (under `__KERNEL__`) that groups all valid expectation flags (`PERMANENT`, `INACTIVE`, `USERSPACE`). This macro is used by the netlink policy to define an allowed mask for the `CTA_EXPECT_FLAGS` attribute.

- **net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_proto_tcp.c**:  
  Changes the `tcp_nla_policy` entries for three TCP info attributes:  
  - `CTA_PROTOINFO_TCP_STATE`: now uses `NLA_POLICY_MAX(NLA_U8, TCP_CONNTRACK_SYN_SENT2)`, rejecting values above the valid state.  
  - `CTA_PROTOINFO_TCP_WSCALE_ORIGINAL` and `CTA_PROTOINFO_TCP_WSCALE_REPLY`: now use `NLA_POLICY_MAX(NLA_U8, TCP_MAX_WSCALE)` (max=14), preventing out-of-range values that could cause undefined behavior as shift counts.  
  Removes the manual `if` check that validated ` >= TCP_CONNTRACK_MAX` for the state attribute, as the policy now handles it.

- **net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_netlink.c**:  
  - **Filter flags**: Changes `CTA_FILTER_ORIG_FLAGS` and `CTA_FILTER_REPLY_FLAGS` from plain `NLA_U32` to `NLA_POLICY_MASK(NLA_U32, CTA_FILTER_F_ALL)`, and removes the manual checks (`if (filter->orig_flags & ~CTA_FILTER_F_ALL)`), allowing the core to reject invalid bits early.  
  - **Expectation flags**: Changes `CTA_EXPECT_FLAGS` from `{ .type = NLA_U32 }` to `NLA_POLICY_MASK(NLA_BE32, NF_CT_EXPECT_MASK)`, validating the flags against the newly defined mask and also switching to big-endian type (`NLA_BE32`) for consistency.

### Relationship between changes:

The modifications are linked by the common goal of centralizing validation in netlink policies:  
- The header file provides the mask macro (`NF_CT_EXPECT_MASK`) used by the `ctnetlink` policy for expectation flags.  
- The TCP protocol file adjusts policies for TCP-specific attributes, relying on `TCP_MAX_WSCALE` and `TCP_CONNTRACK_SYN_SENT2` defined elsewhere (already available).  
- The netlink file removes redundant manual checks for filter and expectation flags, leveraging the new policies to catch invalid values at attribute parsing time.  

All three changes eliminate potential undefined behavior (e.g., shift with out-of-range window scale) and simplify code by relying on the netlink subsystem for validation.

This patch replaces manual range and mask validations in the ctnetlink code path with netlink policy annotations, letting the core reject invalid values early and report extended acknowledgment errors.

## Modifications per file

### 1. `include/uapi/linux/netfilter/nf_conntrack_common.h`
- Added a new macro `NF_CT_EXPECT_MASK` (guarded by `#ifdef __KERNEL__`), which groups all valid expectation flags (`NF_CT_EXPECT_PERMANENT`, `NF_CT_EXPECT_INACTIVE`, `NF_CT_EXPECT_USERSPACE`). This macro is used later in the policy for the `CTA_EXPECT_FLAGS` attribute.

### 2. `net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_netlink.c`
- **Filter flags (`CTA_FILTER_ORIG_FLAGS`, `CTA_FILTER_REPLY_FLAGS`):**  
  - Changed the policy from `NLA_U32` to `NLA_POLICY_MASK(NLA_U32, CTA_FILTER_F_ALL)`. This tells the core to reject any bits outside the valid mask.  
  - Removed the manual `if (filter->orig_flags & ~CTA_FILTER_F_ALL)` checks in `ctnetlink_parse_filter()`, since the policy now enforces the mask.

- **Expect flags (`CTA_EXPECT_FLAGS`):**  
  - Changed the policy from `NLA_U32` to `NLA_POLICY_MASK(NLA_BE32, NF_CT_EXPECT_MASK)`. The new `NF_CT_EXPECT_MASK` from the header defines the allowed bits. Note the type change to `NLA_BE32` (big-endian) to match how these flags are always stored in network byte order.

- **No manual parsing code removed for expect flags**: The policy change is self-contained; there was no manual validation to remove (the original code accepted any `u32`).

### 3. `net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_proto_tcp.c`
- **TCP state (`CTA_PROTOINFO_TCP_STATE`):**  
  - Changed policy from `NLA_U8` to `NLA_POLICY_MAX(NLA_U8, TCP_CONNTRACK_SYN_SENT2)`. This rejects values greater than the last valid state.  
  - Removed the manual check `if (nla_get_u8(tb[CTA_PROTOINFO_TCP_STATE]) >= TCP_CONNTRACK_MAX)` from `nlattr_to_tcp()`, because the policy now catches invalid values.

- **TCP window scale values (`CTA_PROTOINFO_TCP_WSCALE_ORIGINAL`, `CTA_PROTOINFO_TCP_WSCALE_REPLY`):**  
  - Changed policy from `NLA_U8` to `NLA_POLICY_MAX(NLA_U8, TCP_MAX_WSCALE)` (where `TCP_MAX_WSCALE` is 14). This prevents values above 14, which would cause undefined behavior when used as a shift count.  
  - No manual validation existed for these; the policy now provides the missing clamp.

## Relationships between changes
- The new `NF_CT_EXPECT_MASK` macro in the UAPI header is directly referenced by the policy for `CTA_EXPECT_FLAGS`, ensuring that only the defined expectation flags are accepted.  
- All manual range/mask checks that were removed from `ctnetlink_parse_filter()` and `nlattr_to_tcp()` are now redundant thanks to the corresponding netlink policy annotations.  
- The policy-level rejections happen before the kernel parsing functions are called, so the code becomes simpler and error messages are generated automatically by the netlink core.

## Summary of Modifications

### File: `net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_netlink.c`
- **Filter flags policy**: Changed `CTA_FILTER_ORIG_FLAGS` and `CTA_FILTER_REPLY_FLAGS` from plain `NLA_U32` to `NLA_POLICY_MASK(NLA_U32, CTA_FILTER_F_ALL)`, enabling netlink core to reject invalid flag bits automatically.
- **Removed manual checks**: Deleted the runtime validations `if (filter->orig_flags & ~CTA_FILTER_F_ALL)` and its reply counterpart from `ctnetlink_parse_filter()`.
- **Expect flags policy**: Changed `CTA_EXPECT_FLAGS` from `NLA_U32` to `NLA_POLICY_MASK(NLA_BE32, NF_CT_EXPECT_MASK)`, using a new constant for the allowed bits.

### File: `include/uapi/linux/netfilter/nf_conntrack_common.h`
- Added the kernel-side macro `NF_CT_EXPECT_MASK` (inside `#ifdef __KERNEL__`) that groups all valid expectation flags:  
  `NF_CT_EXPECT_PERMANENT | NF_CT_EXPECT_INACTIVE | NF_CT_EXPECT_USERSPACE`.

### File: `net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_proto_tcp.c`
- **TCP state policy**: Changed `CTA_PROTOINFO_TCP_STATE` to `NLA_POLICY_MAX(NLA_U8, TCP_CONNTRACK_SYN_SENT2)`, rejecting values larger than the maximum valid state.
- **Window scale policies**: Changed `CTA_PROTOINFO_TCP_WSCALE_ORIGINAL` and `CTA_PROTOINFO_TCP_WSCALE_REPLY` to `NLA_POLICY_MAX(NLA_U8, TCP_MAX_WSCALE)` (max 14), preventing undefined behavior from using out‑of‑range shift counts.
- **Removed manual state check**: Deleted the runtime validation `if (nla_get_u8(tb[CTA_PROTOINFO_TCP_STATE]) >= TCP_CONNTRACK_MAX)` from `nlattr_to_tcp()`.

### Relationships Between Modifications
All changes pursue a unified goal: **replace manual range/mask checks with netlink policy annotations** so that the netlink core performs early validation and generates proper `extack` error messages.

- The filter flag policies and the TCP policies are independent but follow the same pattern — moving validation from runtime code to the policy table.
- The new `NF_CT_EXPECT_MASK` constant in the header is a prerequisite for the expect flags policy in `nf_conntrack_netlink.c`.
- The TCP state policy uses `TCP_CONNTRACK_SYN_SENT2` (the highest valid state) as the upper bound, while the manual check previously used `TCP_CONNTRACK_MAX` (which includes an extra sentinel value). The policy now correctly limits to the actual maximum valid state.
